Note: Total consensus. The one everyone agrees on.
Most name it; Bootstrap treats it as a plain Button variant.

Description: Persistent primary action floating over content
Note: Material-only coinage. Apple uses a toolbar action instead.

Description: Mutually-exclusive choice rendered as joined buttons
Note: Five words, one pattern (Carbon's 'Content switcher' is the outlier). Polaris/Bootstrap reuse 'Button group' here — colliding with the real Button group. We have --st-segmented-* tokens + a preview card, but no codified Segmented primitive — confirm/codify.

Description: Button that opens a menu of actions
Note: Many words for one control; ARIA's formal 'Menu Button' is the term almost nobody adopts.

Description: Primary action + attached dropdown of related actions
Note: Effectively Bootstrap-only as a named component.
Aligned industry-wide. Not a standalone primitive for us — it's adapter behaviour (<Link to>), so the registry deliberately gives it no story.

Description: Group of related buttons sharing one container
Note: Carbon says 'Button set'; ARIA calls the interactive version a Toolbar. Pink Moon ships it one-word as 'ButtonGroup'.

'Text field' (Material/Apple/Polaris) vs 'Input' (Bootstrap) vs 'Textfield' (Atlassian) — the classic three-way split. CONFIRM (SUG-145): the registry shows a 'comp-inputs' preview/token surface but NO confirmed Storybook story — grep packages/ds/ for an Input component + *.stories.*. If a story exists → In system; if only preview/tokens → To codify, and it's the FIRST dependency of the Form epic. DECISION (SUG-145): canonical name is 'Input', not 'TextField' — the control also hosts email/password/search/number, so 'text' is a false constraint (a password field isn't text); 'type' stays config (<Input type='password'>), never PasswordField/SearchField clones. Keep Textarea a SEPARATE sibling primitive — do not fold multiline into Input as a prop (Material/Polaris do; we don't). The boundary is enforced by HTML semantics (<input> vs <textarea>), so it's non-negotiable, not a style preference; Field composes the two distinctly.
Material & Polaris treat it as a multiline prop, not its own component. POSITION: used inside ContactForm but not codified as a standalone Textarea. Needed to build a generic Form (law 02).
Apple's 'Secure field' is the lone first-class name.
Carbon & Material drop 'field'; Bootstrap has no dedicated search component.

Description: Pick one option from a collapsed list
Note: Six of seven agree on 'Select'; only Apple diverges, calling it a 'Pop-up button' / 'Picker' — a synonym, not a conflict.

Description: Text entry that filters a list of options
Note: 'Autocomplete' (Material) and 'Combobox' (ARIA/Carbon) name the same control.

Description: Suggests completions as the user types
Note: Often the same widget as Combobox; the two terms are used interchangeably.
Apple's 'Stepper' collides with Material's progress 'Stepper' — true false friend.

Description: Drag-and-drop or browse to attach a file
Note: One job, different words: Polaris's 'Drop zone' names the interaction, Carbon's 'File uploader' names the task.
Rare full alignment. Bootstrap leaves it to native input[type=date].
Apple folds time into its Date picker.
Named consistently where it exists, but unevenly supported.
Same widget, no shared name: Apple 'Token field', Material 'Input chip', Ant 'Select (tags)'.
Common in MUI/Ant but absent from most formal systems here.

ANNOTATION: the industry is unanimous on 'Form', but we ship ours as 'ContactForm' (patterns/ContactForm) — a use-case baked into the component name. Rename to a generic 'Form' primitive, or a pattern named by structure, not purpose. The exact error this audit exists to catch. BUILD ORDER (law 02): Form composes Field + Label + Textarea + Helper text + Error message (all now 'To codify') over the existing Input + Button; codify those first, then 'contact' becomes config. ARIA exposes Form as a landmark role.
'Form group' vs 'Form layout' — and Bootstrap just uses its grid.
'Form field' / 'Form group' / 'Field' all wrap one input + its label & error. POSITION: ContactForm wraps each input ad hoc; no codified Field primitive. Needed to build a generic Form (law 02).

Description: Caption guiding input below a field
Note: Five spellings of the same caption: supporting / helper / help / form / helper message. POSITION: used inside ContactForm; not codified. Needed for the Form field anatomy (law 02).

Description: Inline validation error on a field
Note: Carbon's 'Form requirement' and Bootstrap's 'Invalid feedback' are the outliers. POSITION: ContactForm validates inline ad hoc; no codified Error message. Needed for the Form field anatomy (law 02).
Aligned. SwiftUI renders a Toggle as a checkbox on macOS.

Description: Pick one from a set of mutually-exclusive options
Note: Aligned on 'Radio'; ARIA names the wrapping 'Radio Group'.

Description: Instant binary state, often a setting
Note: 'Toggle' is overloaded: Apple/Carbon/Atlassian use it for this on/off switch, but a 'toggle button' elsewhere is a press-and-stay button — two different controls, one word. ANNOTATION: we have no generic Switch/Toggle primitive — only 'ThemeToggle', a use-case-named instance (same anti-pattern as ContactForm). Factor out a primitive.

Description: Pick a value along a continuous track
Note: Two words, one control: Bootstrap & Atlassian say 'Range', everyone else 'Slider'. Not in our DS — earlier 'present' was a mis-file (it confused this audit's own Tweaks slider for a Pink Moon component).
Note the reversal: here 'Range' modifies 'Slider' rather than replacing it.

Description: Discrete selectable token in a set
Note: Two words, one token: 'Chip' (Material) vs 'Tag' (everyone else). The real trap is 'Tag' itself — see the Tag row.
True false friend: 'Tag' is a removable input token in Polaris but a read-only status label in Carbon — two different components, one word.

Six different names — and Apple's 'Navigation bar' means something else to Material (see below). ANNOTATION: 'App bar' is a use-case/positional label — the role name is 'Header' (a banner landmark), which we ship. It is NOT a Toolbar: a Header is a layout region that COMPOSES brand + nav + (optionally) a Toolbar of actions.
Material renamed 'Bottom navigation' → 'Navigation bar', directly clashing with Apple's TOP bar.
Aligned; Apple steers you to a Segmented control instead.
'Drawer' vs 'Sidebar' vs 'Side nav' — and 'Drawer' is itself overloaded (see Side sheet). We ship 'PageSidebar' (content TOC) and 'MobileNav', but no generic primary-nav drawer primitive — confirm.

Description: Slim vertical strip of icon destinations
Note: A Material-3 coinage; no equivalent named elsewhere.

Description: Trail showing location in a hierarchy
Note: Aligned (singular/plural aside). Now codified — DS primitive 'Breadcrumb' (components/Breadcrumb).

Description: Controls for moving between pages of results
Note: Apple's dot-style 'Page control' is the visual & naming outlier. Ours: 'Pagination' (Patterns/Pagination).
Polaris's 'Action list' and Bootstrap's 'Dropdown' describe the same overlay.

Description: Linear multi-step progress through a flow
Note: 'Stepper' here means progress steps — colliding with Apple's increment Stepper.

Description: Jump-links to sections within a long page
Note: ANNOTATION: used all over (PageSidebar TOC, in-page section jump-links) but not codified as its own component — owed a DS/Storybook story. Bootstrap's 'Scrollspy' names the behaviour; Ant calls the component 'Anchor'.
Ubiquitous in tools (⌘K) yet unnamed by every formal system audited.

ARIA & Apple name it cleanly; most web systems compose it ad hoc. ANNOTATION: the reusable control-group primitive (role=toolbar), distinct from the App bar/Header layout region that COMPOSES it. POSITION: our FilterBar instantiates a toolbar ad hoc — no generic Toolbar primitive exists. FUTURE STATE: extract a 'Toolbar' primitive, then re-express FilterBar as a composition of it (law 02).

Description: Focused window over a scrim, blocks page
Note: 'Sheet' is the trap: Apple's 'Sheet' is this modal, but Material's 'Sheet' is a slide-in panel. (Dialog vs Modal alone is just two words for one thing.)
True false friend: Apple's 'Alert' is THIS confirm dialog, but everyone else's 'Alert' is an inline page message — same word, two different components.

Description: Panel sliding up from the bottom edge
Note: Apple's 'Sheet' covers any edge; Material reserves 'Bottom sheet' for the bottom.

Description: Panel sliding in from a side edge
Note: 'Drawer' = nav menu to some, slide-in panel to others. Material splits it as 'Side sheet'.

Description: Small overlay anchored to a trigger
Note: Near-aligned; Atlassian's 'Popup' is the only spelling that drifts.
Aligned across the board.
Snackbar / Toast / Flag / Notification — four words, one transient message.
Scrim / Backdrop / Blanket / Dimming view — same dark veil, four labels. Ours is a token/utility (used by ImageLightbox & modals), not a standalone component.
A positioning primitive (Popper.js) surfacing as a named component in MUI/Atlassian.

Description: Inline contextual message in the page flow
Note: Alert / Banner / Inline notification / Section message — five words for the in-page message. ('Alert' is overloaded — see Confirm dialog.)

Description: Small count or dot on an element
Note: 'Badge' names two different things: a numeric count (Material/Apple/Bootstrap) vs a status label (Polaris). Atlassian keeps them apart — count = 'Badge', status = 'Lozenge'.
Polaris/Bootstrap 'Badge', Carbon 'Tag', Atlassian 'Lozenge' — one status pill, and 'Badge' collides with the numeric-count Badge (see above).
Material 'indicator' & Apple 'view' wrap both linear and circular under one name.
Spinner / Activity indicator / Loading / Circular progress — many words, one busy indicator.

Everyone says 'Skeleton'; only Bootstrap says 'Placeholder' (which also risks colliding with input placeholder text). POSITION: a skeleton ships inside Tile's 'content preview loading' story but isn't factored out. FUTURE STATE: extract a 'Skeleton' primitive, then have Tile (and other loading states) compose it (law 02).
Only Polaris & Atlassian name it as a component; others treat it as a layout.

Description: Gauge of a value within a known range
Note: ARIA 'Meter' vs Apple 'Gauge'; largely absent elsewhere. POSITION: a meter bar ships inside Tile's 'Metric with bar' story, but isn't factored out as its own component. FUTURE STATE: extract a 'Meter' primitive (role=meter, value-in-range), then have Tile compose it (law 02). Confirm it's a true meter, not a progress bar.
'Banner' is near-consistent for the page-level message; only Bootstrap still says 'Alert'.
'Table' vs 'Data table' vs 'Index table' vs 'Dynamic table' — four framings of rows & columns. Ours: DS primitive 'Table' (registry · Primitives/Table).
List / List group / Resource list / Structured list — same rows, four names. No List primitive in our registry (CardGrid / Table cover list-like layouts).
Naming tracks whatever the parent list is called.
Two words, one container: Carbon's 'Tile' is the lone dissenter from the universal 'Card'. ('Tile' is the actual false friend — see the Tile row.)

Description: Square content/metric block, often a grid
Note: Carbon 'Tile' is its Card; Fluent 'Tile' is a launcher square — same word, two meanings. DECISION: strip out Metric/Meter/Skeleton and what's left is a container — i.e. a Card (Carbon proves it: their 'Tile' IS their Card). Fold Tile into Card (a Card variant at most); a 'stat tile' = a Card composing a Metric; the stat/trust section = a CardGrid of those Cards (composite pattern). statTileSection → CardGrid/cardBuilderSection.
Accordion / Expansion panel / Disclosure group / Collapsible all expand-collapse content. Ours: DS primitive 'Accordion' (accordionSection).
Disclosure / Collapse / Collapsible / Expand — the single-panel cousin of Accordion.
Apple's 'Outline' vs everyone's 'Tree'; sparse support overall.

Named consistently where present; absent in core Bootstrap/Carbon. POSITION: in use on person detail pages (e.g. /people/beehead) but no codified Avatar primitive in the DS/Storybook. FUTURE STATE: codify an 'Avatar' primitive, then have the person/metadata surfaces compose it.
'Avatar group' is consistent — but only two systems formalise it.
Ant names it 'Timeline'; still absent from the other six systems.
ANNOTATION: already shipped in Studio/Web as a page-builder section, but not codified in the DS or Storybook. Names are aligned industry-wide ('Carousel'); Apple uses paged scroll + Page control.
ANNOTATION: lives in Studio/Web page-builder sections, not yet codified in the DS or Storybook. Barely named elsewhere — Material's is 'Image list', Ant groups previews under 'Image'.
Mostly just an 'Image'; Polaris formalises the small variant as 'Thumbnail'.
Carbon's 'Code snippet' vs the more common 'Code block'.
Tracks the HTML <dl> element; sometimes 'Definition list'.

DECISION: collapses into Table — a capability tier (display → sortable → editable/virtualized), not a separate component. Industry only splits it out for heavy engines (MUI DataGrid, AG Grid). Avoid the name 'Data grid': 'Grid' is a false friend with the CSS layout Grid and the ARIA grid role. The Table primitive is in system; an editable mode isn't built — add it as a Table variant (role=table read-only → role=grid editable), never a 'DataGrid'.

Ant 'Statistic', others 'Metric'/'KPI'; no formal consensus. POSITION: the metric figure (value + label + trend) lives inside Tile's stories, not factored out. FUTURE STATE: extract a 'Metric' primitive, then have Tile compose it (law 02).
Everyone agrees on 'Grid' for layout — but ARIA 'Grid' is an interactive widget, not layout. Ours: DS primitive 'Grid'.

Rare modern alignment — 'Stack' won, though Apple/Polaris split it by axis. POSITION: the new responsive ButtonGroup view reflows its buttons via Stack — a concrete consumer. DECISION (SUG-Flex): codify ONE 'Stack' primitive and fold Flex into it — do NOT ship a standalone Flex. Stack owns one-axis layout with TOKEN GAP ONLY, plus optional align/justify/wrap and a RESPONSIVE 'direction' prop (e.g. {base:'vertical', md:'horizontal'}) — which is exactly what the responsive ButtonGroup needs. Name it 'Stack' (what it is), not 'Flex' (the implementation). True full-flex needs (grow/shrink ratios) drop to Box + explicit style — a rare, explicit escape hatch, not a generic primitive. ButtonGroup's responsive mode then composes Stack (law 02).

Bootstrap/MUI name it; others bake max-width into page/grid. DECISION (SUG-146): codify 'Container' as its OWN primitive, NOT a prop on Page. Width-constraint recurs at multiple nesting levels (page main region AND individual sections — full-bleed hero vs constrained text in the same page), so it can't live only at the page root. Built on Box; Page COMPOSES Container for its content region (law 02). A 'size' prop encodes the named width tokens (reading 760 / detail 1080 / archive 960) as config; full-bleed = no Container (or size='bleed'). HARD CONSTRAINT: max-width centring lives in Container ONLY — Page must NOT also carry a maxWidth prop (two places to constrain = the drift). Phase 0: grep hardcoded 760/960/1080 + stray max-width+margin-inline:auto; each cluster becomes a Container size token.

A primitives-era component (MUI/Chakra/Polaris); not in classic systems. POSITION: the unstyled style/layout primitive is hand-rolled across content layouts. FUTURE STATE: codify a 'Box' primitive (the token-aware style base the others build on) and audit for drift.

DECISION: not a component for us. SwiftUI/Chakra ship a 'Spacer' component, but we handle spacing as a FOUNDATION — the --st-space-* token scale (foundations/token-reference), consumed via gap/margin. Intentionally absent: spacing tokens ≠ a Spacer component (same don't-conflate-tokens-with-components rule that caught Slider).

'Divider' (UI) vs 'Separator' (ARIA role); Bootstrap just uses <hr>. POSITION: rendered inside PortableText modules & PT-containing sections, but not factored out — today it's the --st-margin-divider rule. FUTURE STATE: codify a 'Divider' primitive (role=separator) that the PT renderer composes (law 02).

Polaris/Atlassian formalise 'Page'; most leave it to the app. POSITION: page scaffolding (gutters, region slots) is repeated across content layouts, not codified. FUTURE STATE: codify a 'Page' primitive — the top-level scaffold (header/main/footer region slots + page gutters). DECISION (SUG-146): Page does NOT own max-width — it COMPOSES Container for its content region (law 02) and carries NO maxWidth prop of its own. Audit existing layouts for drift.

Description: App frame: header + nav + content regions
Note: UI shell / Frame / Page layout / App shell — the same scaffolding, four names. POSITION: header+nav+content scaffolding repeated across content layouts. FUTURE STATE: codify ONE shell primitive (pick the canonical name) and audit for drift.

'Panel' is wildly overloaded (side panel, tab panel, expansion panel, surface). POSITION: generic bordered regions repeated across content layouts. FUTURE STATE: codify — but name by role (Surface / Card / labelled Region), not the vague 'Panel'; audit usages for drift.

Material/Atlassian 'Surface' vs Carbon 'Layer' for elevation backgrounds. POSITION: today an elevation token applied ad hoc across layouts. FUTURE STATE: codify a 'Surface' primitive (elevation container — Material/Atlassian precedent) and audit token usage for drift.

Chakra/Atlassian 'Flex'; Polaris folds it into Stack; Bootstrap as utilities. DECISION (SUG-Flex, resolved): NOT a standalone primitive for us — folds into Stack. 'Flex' names the implementation (flexbox); 'Stack' names what it is (one-axis spacing). A generic Flex re-exposes the full flex API and re-legitimizes the per-call-site gap drift this audit exists to kill; Polaris's no-Flex model is the precedent. The hand-rolled flex wrappers across content layouts migrate to Stack; genuine full-flex control drops to Box + explicit style.
Aligned on 'Icon'; Apple routes glyphs through SF Symbols + Image. We consume lucide-react directly — no Icon wrapper primitive.

Description: Renders children into a different DOM node
Note: A React-era primitive; consistently 'Portal' where exposed.

Description: Content visible only to screen readers
Note: Near-aligned; older code still says 'sr-only'.
Bootstrap's 'Ratio' vs the longer 'Aspect ratio' elsewhere.
Scroll area (Radix) / Scroll view (Apple) / Scrollable (Polaris).

'Label' as a form caption vs Apple's 'Label' (icon+text row) — same word, different jobs. We ship 'SectionLabel' (the mono eyebrow) — a third meaning. POSITION: a form-field label lives inside ContactForm but isn't codified (and isn't SectionLabel). Needed to build a generic Form (law 02).
Tracks the <kbd> element; 'Kbd' vs 'Keyboard key'.

A utility more than a component; named inconsistently. POSITION: card excerpts truncate with ellipsis/line-clamp, ad hoc. FUTURE STATE: codify a 'Truncate' utility/primitive (line-clamp + ellipsis) that Card and PT compose.

Description: Reveals overflowing actions in a menu
Note: The '⋯' menu; Carbon names it, most fold it into Menu/Dropdown. POSITION: cards overflow their tag chips to a '+N more' indicator, ad hoc. NOTE: that chip-overflow ('+N') is distinct from this action-overflow ('⋯') menu — likely two primitives (an overflow indicator vs a Menu). FUTURE STATE: codify both; have Card compose the chip-overflow one.

Apple 'Page control' vs Bootstrap 'Carousel indicators' for the same dots. POSITION: ships inside the Carousel page-builder section but isn't factored out. FUTURE STATE: codify a 'Page control' primitive (role-appropriate dots/index) that the Carousel composes (law 02).
